title: Reduce the forward native snapshot pool from 2,425 banks to 2,106
body:
## Result

A legal serial order of the #7674 forward native graph from aliromman uses **2,106 snapshot banks**, saving 319 against the fixed-order minimum of 2,425 in #7681. Including the shared paid-row accumulator and four scratch fields, the private reservation falls from 2,430 to **2,111 homes per occurrence**, or from 38,880 to **33,776** over 16 disjoint occurrences.

This is a finite allocation certificate with a scoped proof of operator preservation. Among ready rows, the schedule chooses the one that will finish the most donors' remaining reads. Each row retains its exact coefficient list, charts, child and adapters. The new bank is reserved before the first read, all donors survive through child return, and all outputs survive until public installation. The peak is attained at event 3,022, token 94,904. [Proof and contract](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ef52676eb20c252f5786f42a70ef0dd814400a03/research/banked-native-row-order/README.md) · [Generated receipt](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ef52676eb20c252f5786f42a70ef0dd814400a03/research/banked-native-row-order/RESULT.json) · [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19714933)

## Evidence and reproduction

The replay checks 7,643 row events, 9,144 assignments, 169,343 donor reads and 1,501 final outputs against the pinned forward graph. Independent owner counts confirm the peak. Both a live donor/result alias and the assignment restricted to 2,105 banks are rejected. The new schedule pays for all 30,580 full initialization/retirement services per occurrence. The conservative 16-occurrence reset allowance is 11,816,384.

Run from the repository root with any CPython 3.12 interpreter.

```sh
py=python3.12
pkg=research/banked-native-row-order
"$py" -B scripts/research_package.py --package "$pkg"
"$py" -I -B -W error "$pkg/verify.py"
"$py" -I -B -W error -O "$pkg/verify.py"
"$py" -I -B "$pkg/verify.py" --certificate
"$py" -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package "$pkg" --check-source-history --check-modes
```

The certificate command writes the TSV to standard output. Both registered commands passed locally in 0.62 s each on macOS arm64. Output was `PASS_BANKED_NATIVE_ROW_ORDER 2106 banks, 2111 private homes, 169343 reads`. The package and committed-byte, mode and source-history checks passed. The complete TSV hashes to `16de610956122d9f2c68f05d955b5484a0ee31bf201b69546a092495bf97dd86`.

## Limits and credit

The 2,106 lower witness applies to this order and this owner contract. A global schedule optimum and a concrete packed-tape implementation remain open. The proof uses the published row semantics and the five inherited framework assumptions. Physical child operators, the full caller, the selected cold replay and a formal proof were outside the local checks. There is no new κ.

This allocation was produced by Nick Petalas. aliromman posed the question and supplied the fixed-order allocation, fifteen pivots and field-level cost contract. SYLforge supplied the underlying word and caller. Clear1nsight supplied the public comparator encoding and digest. The package retains the original source notices. [Credits and graph provenance](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/ef52676eb20c252f5786f42a70ef0dd814400a03/research/banked-native-row-order/README.md#inputs-and-credit)

## Related open work

- #7669 supplies the parent native word and caller.
- #7674 defines the precise fifteen-pivot graph whose rows are reordered here.
- #7680 computes product and snapshot grid sizes on the same graph under its scalar arithmetic contract.
- #7681 proves the 2,425-bank minimum in the original order and asks whether another legal order can use less storage.
- #7682 publishes the comparator graph digest used here and a separate role-230 graph with changed dependencies.
- #7687 builds reversible CLEAR circuits and distinguishes logical resets from the number of simultaneously reserved banks.
- #7697 reports a chart-595 lifetime split on the role-230 descendant.
- #7704 changes the role-1256 relay on the nine-swap descendant.
- #7705 reroutes hubs on the chart-595 graph and accounts for the reservation on that graph.
- #7708 recodes relay cuts on the role-1256 descendant.
- #7712 prices private homes on its three-split graph.
- #7725 computes a physical prefix range on the role-1256 descendant. Its quantity is scalar amplitude.

## Open next questions

1. Which donors and terminal outputs must coexist in every legal topological order? A lower bound from such a cut would constrain further reductions.
2. What packed backing and movement does this order require with the actual bank views, guards and suspended owners?
